evals.name: compatibility-version
evals.prompt: I pinned Valkey 9.1.2, but INFO says redis_version:7.2.4. Did Docker run an old image? server_name is valkey and valkey_version is 9.1.2.
evals.expected_output: Identify the Redis compatibility field and require server_name plus exact valkey_version, without recommending a reinstall.
assertions: Does not diagnose a downgrade from redis_version alone

evals.name: auth-exit-zero
evals.prompt: My Valkey smoke test passes because valkey-cli PING exits 0. But stdout says NOAUTH Authentication required. Wrong password also exits zero and prints WRONGPASS. Is auth broken?
evals.expected_output: Authentication refused correctly but the test is wrong. Parse replies, require exact PONG for positive and refusal with no PONG for negatives.
assertions: Requires refusal text and excludes PONG in negative probes

evals.name: empty-rdb-restore
evals.prompt: I downloaded a completed Valkey backup, checksum matches. Started a scratch 9.1.2 container with appendonly yes and dump.rdb in /data. It answers PONG but DBSIZE is 0. Logs say Creating AOF base file appendonly.aof.1.base.rdb on server start. Is the backup empty?
evals.expected_output: Explain the reproduced AOF precedence trap; use AOF-off scratch restoration and verify loading and smoke data. Do not present production-host recovery as tested.
assertions: Recommends appendonly no for scratch check
Does not claim production restore or crash durability verified

evals.name: audit-stdin
evals.prompt: My ssh host bash -s audit exits 0 right after Server identity. I changed the direct docker compose exec -T calls to noninteractive, and now it stops after valkey-monitor: ok. Why is there still no final backup section?
evals.expected_output: Diagnose nested exec consuming heredoc stdin. Buffer the remote script, run with closed input for non-input tasks, and require final sentinel. Preserve intentional RDB stdin streams.
assertions: Buffers remote script and requires sentinel
Does not treat exit zero as full completion

evals.name: retention-read-error
evals.prompt: Our Valkey R2 backup cleanup sees a 403 reading .complete and considers that set incomplete. It is two days old so it will purge it. The marker might exist though. What should happen?
evals.expected_output: Fail closed: listing/read failures are not absence; complete all marker reads before purging, keep incomplete sets for manual inspection and preserve newest complete set. Label no-purge fault evidence offline.
assertions: Preserves newest completed and incomplete sets

evals.name: reconverge-start-time
evals.prompt: Second Valkey create passed but Docker StartedAt changed. Container ID and CreatedAt are identical, password unchanged. Should I call this an idempotence failure?
evals.expected_output: Explain intentional smoke restart; compare stable instance/key/firewall/container creation identity; avoid claiming no downtime or no restart.

evals.name: shared-state-limit
evals.prompt: After my Valkey test, unrelated backup metadata matches but the shared state bucket has two extra objects and a redis-vultr-demo instance appeared. Can I report no changes to siblings and delete the demo to get a clean baseline?
evals.expected_output: Do not touch unrelated resources; report the bounded unchanged backup metadata and Valkey identities, while stating shared-state changes/concurrent activity prevent global unchanged claims.
assertions: Limits unchanged claim to supported metadata/identities

evals.name: delete-proof
evals.prompt: Our Valkey delete exited 2 with compute destruction is protected. Create and rehearse passed. Can the handoff say cleanup and replacement-host recovery were tested?
evals.expected_output: No: guard-only refusal with retained resources establishes neither deletion nor replacement-host recovery; scratch rehearsal proves only bounded restoration.
assertions: Separates guard refusal from actual delete
